summary: PostgreSQL database indexes on the executions_visibility table bloat to many times the actual table size in high-volume workflows due to NULL-heavy btree indexes accumulating dead entries. REINDEX temporarily resolves the issue, but partial indexes are needed for permanent fix.
userImpact: Database disk usage grows uncontrollably in high-volume deployments even with retention policies, forcing infrastructure expansion and increased costs.
rootCause: PostgreSQL btree indexes include NULL values, so nullable search-attribute columns in composite indexes accumulate dead entries for every workflow. VACUUM cannot compact these entries; only REINDEX can.
proposedFix: Convert selected nullable btree indexes to partial indexes with WHERE <attribute_column> IS NOT NULL clause to prevent indexing NULL values.
workaround: Run REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY executions_visibility to compact indexes (halves index size), though this must be repeated as bloat reoccurs.
keyQuote: PostgreSQL btree indexes include NULL values. That means mostly-unused generated/custom search-attribute columns still get index entries for every workflow row.
